results.title: Generic Congressional Ballot 2026: Who Leads the House Race

results.content:
Share

Washington, D.C., October 26, 2026 – An Ipsos analysis of the October Reuters/Ipsos Core Political survey conducted October 22-26 finds that the Democratic Party holds a 9-point edge over the Republican Party among likely voters on the 2026 generic congressional ballot. Overall, 53% of likely voters say they would vote for or lean to the Democratic candidate in their district, compared with 44% who say they would vote for or lean to the Republican candidate.

results.content:
This is part of a larger report on the attitudes and dynamics shaping the 2026 midterm elections.

With several weeks to go until Election Day, Americans who are registered to vote favor Democrats over Republicans in the national race for the House of Representatives by an 8 percentage point margin (44% to 36%). About two-in-ten registered voters say they would vote for a third-party candidate or are not sure.
